bio: George Frederick Root (1820–1895) was an American songwriter and composer.

Poems of American History gathers verse on events from the Norse voyages to the Spanish-American War, arranged by historical chapter. The poem here is “The Battle-Cry of Freedom”; Stevenson's editorial headnotes are not reproduced.

poems.title: The Battle-Cry of Freedom
poems.author: George Frederick Root
poems.text:
Yes, we'll rally round the flag, boys, we'll rally once again,
  Shouting the battle-cry of freedom,
We will rally from the hill-side, we'll gather from the plain,
  Shouting the battle-cry of freedom.
Chorus--The Union forever, hurrah! boys, hurrah!
      Down with the traitor, up with the star,
    While we rally round the flag, boys, rally once again,
      Shouting the battle-cry of freedom.

We are springing to the call of our brothers gone before,
  Shouting the battle-cry of freedom,
And we'll fill the vacant ranks with a million freemen more,
  Shouting the battle-cry of freedom.

We will welcome to our numbers the loyal, true, and brave,
  Shouting the battle-cry of freedom,
And altho' they may be poor, not a man shall be a slave,
  Shouting the battle-cry of freedom.

So we're springing to the call from the East and from the West,
  Shouting the battle-cry of freedom,
And we'll hurl the rebel crew from the land we love the best,
  Shouting the battle-cry of freedom.
